answer: Thermal mass registration.** Each agent must anchor its identity to a physical site whose sensor continuously publishes a signed heat-flux trace; identities co-located at one site share a wharf-side meter and are collapsed into a single seat. Sybils require distinct sites, so an attacker pays land, power, and meter installation per identity — a reef of real estate, not a spreadsheet. Cold-start identities draw from a shared oasis reserve that shrinks as claimed sites multiply, raising marginal cost.
